input_and_context: RFC requirements, repository code, semantic summaries, and call relations
llm_decision: Build hierarchical code summaries; localize requirement-relevant code; request missing caller or callee context; review a candidate against the RFC
runtime_and_fixed_control: A finite-state detection workflow exposes Query, Query_Callee, and Query_Caller tools; repository traversal and retrieval are runtime-controlled
state_feedback_and_recovery: The semantic index persists repository context; the detection state carries the requirement and prior reasoning; a self-criticism validation step can reject a candidate
extraction_note: The paper reports aggregate developer responses and patches, but the study-level label remains candidate judgment because item-level public alignment is not established.

input_and_context: Package profile JSON, source code, compact CodeQL schema, generated-query results, and trace context
llm_decision: The Query agent synthesizes or repairs CodeQL; the Review agent assesses reachability and exploitability; the Sanitize agent issues a clean-slate verdict
runtime_and_fixed_control: CodeQL compiles and runs locally; fixed trace_flow and sandboxed grep/snippet tools retrieve bounded evidence
state_feedback_and_recovery: Compiler stderr is placed in an ephemeral retry context for up to three attempts; exhaustion returns control to the main thread to revise or discard the hypothesis
principal_output: Query provenance, reviewed findings, PoC-oriented material, and item-level public traces for disclosed cases
extraction_note: The three-agent separation and bounded compilation loop are reported design elements; public alignment applies only to individually mapped findings.

input_and_context: Contract ABI and source context, transaction sequences, instruction coverage, data dependencies, behavioral indicators, and coverage gaps
llm_decision: Generate hierarchical multi-transaction seeds; initialize mutation priors; synthesize recovery seeds when exploration stagnates
runtime_and_fixed_control: A fixed EVM fuzzing loop, bandit scheduler, bug oracles, and selective symbolic-execution worker perform high-throughput execution
state_feedback_and_recovery: Coverage and dependency feedback update scheduling; a compact stagnation summary triggers asynchronous LLM reseeding while symbolic execution explores constrained branches
principal_output: Runtime safety signals and benchmark vulnerability detections
source_location: Paper Sec. IV-A--IV-D and V-C, Fig. 3, Tables VII--X, pp. 3285--3294
extraction_note: The LLM supplies semantic seeds and priors; the fuzzer, scheduler, symbolic executor, sandbox, and oracles remain separate execution components.

input_and_context: Target source, call graph, reachability constraints, corpus status, debugger observations, and prior attempts
llm_decision: Infer preconditions and root causes; produce trigger plans and a property-based input generator; diagnose path divergence or unmet trigger constraints
runtime_and_fixed_control: A PLAN--IMPLEMENT--EXECUTE--REFLECT state machine invokes stateless MCP tools for code search, corpus inspection, property-based execution, deviation detection, and debugging
state_feedback_and_recovery: A persistent Markdown state stores hypotheses, constraints, plans, solver artifacts, evidence, and failed attempts; REFLECT revises the next plan after execution failure
principal_output: PoV-oriented reproducible trigger on evaluated benchmark targets
extraction_note: The persistent state and phase-specific tool permissions are explicit; the reported result concerns known benchmark targets rather than open-world discovery.

input_and_context: AFL++ crash input, instrumented binary, generated exploit script, stdout, stderr, and return code
llm_decision: Generate an exploit from the crash context; interpret failed execution logs; revise the script; explain a validated exploit
runtime_and_fixed_control: An MCP server runs generated Python scripts against the target binary, captures outputs, enforces a loop limit, and forwards validated material to the analyzer
state_feedback_and_recovery: Failed execution logs and the previous script are returned to the generator for bounded refinement; human intervention is possible after the limit
principal_output: Executed Python PoC and explanatory report
extraction_note: The fuzzer supplies the original crash; the system validates generated scripts against the evaluated binaries rather than claiming independent vulnerability discovery.

input_and_context: A fixed npm package version, package source, structured candidate hypotheses, inferred constraints, exploit attempts, and class-specific oracle feedback
llm_decision: Finder enumerates candidates; Judge filters exploitability; Constraints Inferencer states entry points and payload conditions; Exploiter revises executable PoCs
runtime_and_fixed_control: A custom staged runtime restricts source/search tools by stage, executes Node.js and shell commands, records stdout/stderr, and applies class-specific side-effect oracles
state_feedback_and_recovery: Each stage has isolated context and typed outputs; exploit attempts are bounded, failed attempts are retained, and up to three runs are allowed when no exploit succeeds
extraction_note: The paper separates LLM reasoning stages from the execution harness and automated oracles; manual review can still reject oracle-passing PoCs.

input_and_context: Target host, reconnaissance output, service and version inventory, online search results, exploit repositories, and prior execution history
llm_decision: Reconnaissance selects commands; Search summarizes attack surfaces and exploit procedures; Planning ranks version-matched options; Execution adapts procedures and diagnoses errors
runtime_and_fixed_control: Four agents call reconnaissance and search tools, retrieve from RAG databases, prepare exploit dependencies, and execute commands in isolated target environments
state_feedback_and_recovery: Environmental, attack-surface, and exploit databases persist state across stages; execution errors and code are recorded for self-reflection and to avoid repeated failures
principal_output: Controlled penetration-testing stage completion and exploitation summary
extraction_note: The workflow operates on CVE-grounded vulnerable environments and CTF tasks; task completion is not evidence of new vulnerability discovery.

input_and_context: OSS-Fuzz project configuration, source snapshot, seeds, bug candidates, PoVs, patches, tests, and per-CRS resource budgets
llm_decision: Integrated CRS components may use LLM calls for analysis or patch tasks; the OSS-CRS paper primarily specifies how those components are deployed and composed
runtime_and_fixed_control: Prepare/build-target/run phases execute in isolated Docker containers; LiteLLM routes models and enforces budgets; libCRS and sidecars validate and exchange artifacts
state_feedback_and_recovery: File-backed shared directories persist seeds, PoVs, patches, and candidates; patch checking applies a patch, rebuilds, reruns the PoV, and runs tests
extraction_note: OSS-CRS is an orchestration framework rather than one uniform LLM decision policy; its mechanism row therefore separates framework controls from integrated CRS-specific reasoning.
